{"id":"mimid-1wgh.37.106","title":"wg: mimi-content has no call-endpoint semantics, and we have never raised it","description":"Mark, 2026-11-23: "the ietf mimi specs are pretty weak about vtc
endpoints, i cant remember if we raised emails, issues, or PRs against
the mimi IDs about it."

CHECKED THE RECORD: we have not. Nothing was raised.
- Beads: the only VTC mentions are mimid-bcji (our own binding draft,
  filed today), mimid-7yn7.5 (content coverage, which lists
  "Voice/video calls | Largely outside mimi-content; a core feature of
  every app on the list"), and two coland interop beads that mention it
  only in passing. No bead labelled `wg` about it, and nothing under
  epic mimid-1wgh.37 before this one.
- IETF notes (/data/PROJECT/IETF/notes): the only matches for `vtc` or
  `teleconference` are inside an IETF 127 **aipref** meeting transcript,
  a different working group, where the words are coincidental. No mimi
  list post, no GitHub issue, no PR.

So this is unraised, and Mark's reading that the specs are weak here
matches what the code had to invent.

WHAT MIMI GIVES US, as far as the drafts go: mimi-content has a
`session` disposition and §4.5 ExternalPart, and that is about all. The
drafts say nothing about:
- what a receiver does with a `session` part it cannot join (no scheme
  negotiation, no capability advertisement, no refusal shape);
- whether a `session` part is content to be fetched or a live endpoint
  to be dialled -- mimid decided the latter and never fetches one, but
  nothing says so;
- lifetime: whether the endpoint is still live, who ends it, whether a
  later message supersedes it. An ExternalPart has `expires`, which is
  about the URL's availability rather than a call's;
- which URL schemes are meaningful. mimid takes https and wss and puts
  anything else in the body, which is a guess;
- ringing, declining, joining, or who is already in the call -- the
  states every app on Mark's gatekeeper list has.

WHAT MIMID DID ABOUT IT, which is the evidence for a WG post: it mapped
the `session` disposition to a JMAP MessageAction of type
`urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:cap:vtc` in both directions
(project.rs:202-210, backend.rs:872-893), choosing the scheme set and
the never-fetch rule itself. That is an implementation report the WG can
use: here is what one implementation had to decide because the draft did
not.

PROPOSED, and it needs Mark's OK before anything is posted, per
AGENTS.md and the peer-contributing rules:
1. A mimi-content issue or list post asking what a receiver is expected
   to do with a `session` part, with mimid's choices as the concrete
   case. That is a question, not a proposal, and is the cheapest first
   move.
2. If the WG is interested, a draft section or a separate extension for
   call signalling. Note bead mimid-7yn7.5's observation that calls are
   "largely outside mimi-content", so this may be a separate document
   rather than a patch.
3. Either way, specify the mapping in our own
   draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00 first (bead mimid-bcji), so our
   implementation stops being ahead of its own specification.

Doing (3) before (1) is the better order: it makes the question concrete
and shows we have implemented something rather than only asking.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-23T18:15:14.084037478Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-23T18:15:14.084037478Z","labels":["wg"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.37.106","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.37","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-23T18:15:14.784189346Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"CORRECTED 2026-11-23. Mark: "doesnt the spec have something already,
just weakly specified?" He is right, and my description above undersold
it. Read the actual text rather than characterising it.

WHAT MIMI-CONTENT-10 ACTUALLY HAS:

1. A NAMED SECTION: §5.10 "Conferencing" (txt line 1796).
2. The `session` disposition, value 7, in the IANA Content Disposition
   Values registry (§line 2326: "a description of a multimedia session,
   or URI"). Note it covers BOTH an SDP-style DESCRIPTION and a join
   URI; I had only noted the URI.
3. A COMPLETE WORKED EXAMPLE, lines 1804-1835: the CBOR of a
   conferencing message, topicId "Foo 118", an ExternalPart with
   disposition 7, cardinality 2 (external), url
   "https://example.com/join/12345", description "Join the Foo 118
   conference".
4. Two described approaches: the URL "could be rendered to the user,
   requiring a click. Alternatively the URL could be in an ExternalPart
   with a disposition of session, which could be processed differently
   by the client (for example, alerting the user or presenting a dialog
   box)."

AND THE SENTENCE THAT EXPLAINS THE WEAKNESS, §5.10: "Further discussion
of calling and conferencing functionality is out-of-scope of this
document."

So it is not an omission. It is an explicit scope boundary, and
everything inside it is "could", never MUST or SHOULD: nothing
interoperable is specified.

THIS ALSO VINDICATES MIMID'S CHOICES rather than making them inventions:
- Mapping a session part to a JMAP VTC MessageAction so the client can
  show a join affordance IS §5.10's "alerting the user or presenting a
  dialog box". mimid is implementing the spec's own suggestion.
- The never-fetch rule has implicit support in the example, which nulls
  every content-fetch field: expires 0, size 0, encAlg none, hashAlg
  none. A session ExternalPart is plainly not content to download.

CHECKED AND NOTHING FURTHER EXISTS: draft-mimi-content-more-extensions-01
covers sender timestamp, external message ID, subject and lastSeen
ordering. Nothing about calling.

SO THE WG POSTURE CHANGES, and for the better. Not "you forgot
something" but: §5.10 deliberately defers calling, here is what one
implementation had to decide in the gap, and here is the interop
consequence. Concretely, what two implementations cannot agree on
today while staying conformant:
- whether a session part is rendered as a link or acted on;
- which URL schemes carry (mimid takes https and wss);
- whether the DESCRIPTION form, the other half of the disposition's
  definition, is expected at all -- mimid handles only the URI form;
- what a receiver that cannot join does;
- lifetime, ringing, declining, who is present.

The question for the WG is whether calling should come into scope, and
mimid's implementation is the evidence for asking. Posting still needs
Mark's OK."}
